units.function: Static CLI formatter registry for eleven named vendor/local/gateway adapter types plus generic process/http adapters, with unknown types silently falling back to the process formatter.
units.dependencyDirection: The central registry imports every first-party adapter's CLI formatter directly, constructs local CLIAdapterModule wrappers and stores them in a string-keyed Map. CLI consumers call getCLIAdapter through the facade.
units.keyDataModels: Unversioned adapter type strings and CLIAdapterModule containing formatStdoutEvent.
units.lifecycle: Load every formatter at CLI startup/module import; build type map; resolve requested string; return matching formatter or generic process fallback.
units.testAssessment: No focused registry tests were found. CLI no-emit TypeScript passed on 2026-08-19. Static source proves the registered set and fallback, but duplicate types, unknown-type behavior, optional-package failure, tree-shaking/startup cost, parser errors and capability/version compatibility are unverified.
units.designRationale: Give the monolithic CLI one simple lookup over built-in provider-specific stream presentation while retaining a permissive fallback for external/unknown runtime output.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must allow Raft Agent, Codex, DeepSeek and enterprise Agents to connect through equal independently versioned Connector packages without central vendor imports or silent semantic degradation.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as a Connector package discovery/registration boundary separate from CLI presentation. Use signed package manifests, stable protocol/version negotiation, capability declarations, deployment compatibility and explicit unsupported errors. Dynamically load only installed/allowed adapters; normalized server events feed Company OS Web/CLI renderers. Never let vendor formatter types enter core/application.
units.responsibilityConflict: Formatter lookup has no responsibility semantics, but silently mapping an unknown runtime to process output can erase vendor/protocol identity and make unparsed stdout appear valid evidence from the wrong Connector.

securityFindings: Unknown adapter types silently fall back to raw process formatting instead of failing closed, concealing protocol/configuration errors and bypassing expected parsing/redaction.
Every vendor formatter package is statically imported, expanding the CLI dependency/supply-chain and startup surface even when a Connector is unused.
Type keys are unversioned strings with no protocol/capability/schema/compatibility negotiation or duplicate-registration guard.
No package signature, provenance, license, allowlist, sandbox or deployment-profile policy appears at registry lookup.
Formatter exceptions, malicious output, parser version drift and safe fallback/degraded-state signaling are untested.
Registry centralization makes every new vendor a core CLI code change, conflicting with equal third-party/enterprise Connector ownership and independent upgrades.
